newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerian police arrest suspected Shi'ite Moslems.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian police arrest suspected Shi'ite Moslems.

text.p: Police in the northern state of Kaduna have arrested seven suspected members of a Shi'ite Moslem group for breach of the peace, a day after 43 Moslems were detained in another northern state.
"We arrested the seven of them while carrying posters with inciting inscriptions," police commissioner Alhaji Umar said on Saturday, quoted by the News Agency of Nigeria on Sunday.

"One of the posters read: 'Ta addancin gwamnati akan Musulmi,' meaning: 'Bad doings of government on Muslims,'" Umar said, adding that the posters bore the photograph of arrested Shi'ite leader Ibrahim El-Zak-Zaky and other members.
On Saturday, the agency reported that police in Sokoto state, also in the north, arrested 43 members of the same group for planning to breach peace in the area.

In September, two police and five Shi'ites were killed in northern Nigeria when supporters of the fundamentalist Shi'ite Moslem Brothers group clashed with the police while demanding the release of their arrested leader, Sheikh Ibrahim Yakub El-Zak-Zaky.
El-Zak-Zaky, a radical preacher, was arrested because of illegal publications and radio broadcasts, the police said. He was also alleged to have imported arms. He is still in detention.
The group is campaigning for the imposition of Islamic Sharia law in Africa's most populous nation, although only about half the 100 million people are Moslems, mainly of the Sunni sect.
